title: Explainable Kernel Scorer & Autotuner for Burst-Aware Prefill/Decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight, explainable kernel scoring layer and online autotuner that: 1) ranks candidate kernels per-request using an interpretable score (latency tail, cost, memory headroom, and correctness proxy), 2) adapts weights by seqlen/architecture buckets and burstiness signals, and 3) provides audit trails so rollouts and fallbacks are explainable to SRE/PM teams. This ticket covers design and first-stage implementation: offline cost-model fitting, seqlen bucketing, runtime scorer proto, telemetry hooks, and a staged canary rollout with safe fallback to the existing kernel chooser.
acceptance_criteria: A explainable scoring function is implemented and logged per decision (feature weights+score)
Offline cost/latency model that predicts relative kernel rank across three seqlen buckets (<64, 64-512, >512) for GPU families (A100, H100) is trained and stored
Autotuner can update feature weights online using exponential moving average with a conservative learning rate and be rolled back during canary
End-to-end canary on 10% traffic demonstrates <=5% regression in p99 latency and >=3% token-cost reduction for mixed conversational workload
Telemetry dashboard links kernel decisions to end-to-end latency and cost; audit log retained for 30 days
implementation_steps: 1) Define feature set for scorer: estimated token compute, memory-occupancy-margin, kv-cache-effectiveness, recent tail-latency residual, model-compatibility-penalty
2) Build offline microbench harness to collect per-kernel metrics across seqlen/arch combos
3) Fit simple linear/explainable model (LASSO + feature normalization) and produce initial weights
4) Instrument runtime scorer to return score + top-3 candidate kernels and emit decision event to telemetry
5) Implement conservative online weight update: EMWA with clamped weight deltas and minimum confidence threshold
6) Add safety net: rollback window and immediate fallback to legacy chooser on p95/p99 SLA breach
7) Create canary config and run 10% traffic experiment for 2 weeks with daily reviews
8) Iterate on weight priors and expand seqlen buckets if needed
benchmarks: expected-savings-note: estimator predicts 2-6% token-cost reduction for chat workloads with 1.5-2.5x variance bursts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: model overfits to offline microbench; Mitigation: add field validation and a conservative online learning rate
Risk: explainability exposes internal heuristics; Mitigation: redact absolute model internals and only surface normalized feature weights
Risk: noisy telemetry during rollout triggers false rollbacks; Mitigation: require sustained SLA breach over 30 minutes before triggering automatic fallback
